results.title: Isomorphism-closed class of groups
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A class of groups $X$ is a property of groups that is invariant under isomorphism: if a group $H$ belongs to $X$ and $K$ is a group isomorphic to $H$, then $K$ belongs to $X$.

results.title: Quotient lying in a class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a class of groups $X$, a group $G$ and a subgroup $N$ of $G$, this holds when $N$ is normal in $G$ and the quotient group $G/N$ belongs to $X$.

results.title: Formation of finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class of groups $X$ is a formation if it contains the trivial group, for every finite group $G$ in $X$ and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ the quotient $G/N$ belongs to $X$, and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $N_1, N_2$ such that $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ belong to $X$, the quotient $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ belongs to $X$.

results.title: Radical (Fitting) class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class of groups $X$ is radical if, for every finite group $G$, every normal subgroup of $G$ belongs to $X$ whenever $G$ does, and whenever $N_1, N_2$ are normal subgroups of $G$ that belong to $X$, their product $N_1 N_2$ belongs to $X$.

results.title: Hereditary class of groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class of groups $X$ is hereditary if every subgroup of a finite group in $X$ belongs to $X$.

results.title: Soluble radical
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $R$ of a group $G$ is the soluble radical of $G$ if $R$ is a soluble normal subgroup of $G$ that contains every soluble normal subgroup of $G$.

results.title: Solubly saturated class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class of groups $X$ is solubly saturated (a composition class) if, for every finite group $G$ with soluble radical $R$, whenever the Frattini subgroup $\Phi(R)$ of $R$ is normal in $G$ and $G/\Phi(R)$ belongs to $X$, the group $G$ belongs to $X$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 12.7 (Vasil'ev)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every radical hereditary formation of finite groups is a composition formation: every class of groups that is a formation, a radical class and a hereditary class is solubly saturated.

results.title: Radical hereditary formations need not be composition formations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not true that every radical hereditary formation of finite groups is a composition formation: some class of groups that is a formation, a radical class and a hereditary class is not solubly saturated.

results.title: The $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ satisfies the $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence if $F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2} + \dots + F_{n-m}$ for every integer $n$, that is, $F_n = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} F_{n-i-1}$. For $m = 0$ this says $F_n = 0$ for all $n$.

reading_title.source: The $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence

results.title: The standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ is the standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence if it satisfies the $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence, $F_i = 0$ for every natural number $i < m - 1$, and $F_{m-1} = 1$, where $m - 1$ is computed in the integers.

results.title: Weighted sum of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$, a natural number $m$, integers $N$ and $l$, and a rational number $q$, $S(m,N,l,q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} q^k F_{k+l}$; for $N < 0$ this is the empty sum $0$.

results.title: First-moment weighted sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$, a natural number $m$, integers $N$ and $l$, and a rational number $q$, $S_2(m,N,l,q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} k q^k F_{k+l}$; for $N < 0$ this is the empty sum $0$. The value does not depend on $m$.

results.title: Shifted self-convolution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ and natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the shifted self-convolution is $w_n^{(m)} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+m-1} F_{n-j+m-1}$, with the indices computed in the integers.

results.title: Fibonacci numbers at integer indices
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For an integer $n$, $F_n$ is the $n$-th Fibonacci number as a rational number: $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$ for $n \ge 0$, and $F_{-n} = (-1)^{n+1} F_n$ for $n > 0$.

results.title: Fibonacci self-convolution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $v_n$ is the rational number $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).

results.title: Even part of the Fibonacci self-convolution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $E_n$ is the rational number $\sum F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, the sum taken over the even integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).

results.title: Odd part of the Fibonacci walk count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the sum of $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the odd $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$, where $F_k$ are the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$). It is the part of $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ that comes from odd $j$.

results.title: Recurrence for the shifted self-convolution of higher-order Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a sequence of rational numbers with $F_n = F_{n-1} + \dots + F_{n-m}$ for every integer $n$, $F_i = 0$ for $0 \le i < m - 1$ and $F_{m-1} = 1$, and for $n \ge 0$ let $w_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+m-1} F_{n-j+m-1}$. Then for every integer $n \ge 0$, $(m+1) w_{n+1} - 2m w_n = (n+m+2) F_{n+m} - (n+m) F_{n+m-1}$.

results.title: Even and odd parts of the Fibonacci self-convolution agree at odd length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. For every integer $k \ge 1$, $E_{2k-1} = O_{2k-1}$.

results.title: Even and odd parts of the Fibonacci self-convolution at even length
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Halving the Fibonacci self-convolution at odd length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, and let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of the same terms $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. results.title: Halving the Fibonacci self-convolution at even length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, and let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of the same terms $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. results.title: F. and M. Riesz theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a complex Borel measure on the circle $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. If $\int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{2\pi i n z} \, d\mu(z) = 0$ for every integer $n \ge 1$, then $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{T}$.

results.title: Fatou's theorem on radial limits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic and bounded on the open unit disc $|z| < 1$. Then for Lebesgue-almost every $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ the radial limit $\lim_{r \to 1^-} f(r e^{i\theta})$ exists in $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Besicovitch's Kakeya set of measure zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a compact set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of Lebesgue measure zero that contains a unit segment in every direction: $K$ is measurable, and for every unit vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^2$ there is a point $a \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $a + t v \in K$ for all $t \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa theorem over $\mathbb{F}_2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a nonempty subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let $K$ be a real number such that the sumset $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$ satisfies $|A + A| \le K |A|$. results.title: Feasible flow
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set, $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function and $s, t \in V$. A function $f : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ if $0 \le f(u, v) \le c(u, v)$ for all $u, v \in V$ and $f$ is conserved at every vertex $v \ne s, t$, that is, $\sum_{u \in V} f(u, v) = \sum_{w \in V} f(v, w)$.

results.title: Flow value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$, a vertex $s \in V$ and a function $f : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$, the value of $f$ is its net outflow from the source $s$, $\sum_{v \in V} f(s, v) - \sum_{u \in V} f(u, s)$.

results.title: Source–sink cut
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $V$ and vertices $s, t \in V$, an $s$-$t$ cut is a subset $S \subseteq V$ with $s \in S$ and $t \notin S$.

results.title: Cut capacity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set and $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function. The capacity of a subset $S \subseteq V$ is the total capacity of the arcs leaving $S$, $\sum_{u \in S} \sum_{v \in V \setminus S} c(u, v)$.

results.title: Weak duality for flows and cuts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set, $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function and $s, t \in V$. If $f$ is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ and $S$ is an $s$-$t$ cut, then the flow value of $f$ is at most the capacity of $S$ for $c$.

results.title: Max-flow min-cut theorem

results.title: The ε-NFA with no states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Over an alphabet $\alpha$, this is the ε-NFA whose set of states is empty; consequently it has no start states, no accepting states and no transitions.

results.title: One-state automaton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ε-NFA over the alphabet $\alpha$ with a single state, which is both its start state and its accepting state, and no moves at all (neither letter moves nor ε-moves).

results.title: Single-letter automaton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a letter $a$ of the alphabet $\alpha$, this is the ε-NFA over $\alpha$ with two states, a start state and an accepting state, and a single move, which reads $a$ and goes from the start state to the accepting state; it has no other moves and no ε-moves.

results.title: Union of ε-NFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given ε-NFAs $M$ with state set $\sigma$ and $N$ with state set $\tau$ over the same alphabet, their union is the ε-NFA on the disjoint union $\sigma \sqcup \tau$ whose moves are the moves of $M$ and the moves of $N$, whose start states are the start states of $M$ and of $N$, and whose accepting states are the accepting states of $M$ and of $N$.

results.title: Concatenation of ε-NFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given ε-NFAs $M$ with state set $\sigma$ and $N$ with state set $\tau$ over the same alphabet, their concatenation is the ε-NFA on the disjoint union $\sigma \sqcup \tau$ whose moves are the moves of $M$, the moves of $N$, and an ε-move from every accepting state of $M$ to every start state of $N$. Its start states are the start states of $M$ and its accepting states are the accepting states of $N$.

results.title: Kleene star of an ε-NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an ε-NFA $M$ with state set $\sigma$, its star automaton has the states of $M$ together with one new state $q_0$, which is its only start state and its only accepting state. Its moves are the moves of $M$, an ε-move from $q_0$ to every start state of $M$, and an ε-move from every accepting state of $M$ to $q_0$.

results.title: States of Thompson's automaton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The state set $S(r)$ of Thompson's automaton of a regular expression $r$ is defined by structural recursion: $S(0)$ is empty, $S(\varepsilon)$ has one element, $S(a)$ has two elements for a letter $a$, both $S(P + Q)$ and $S(PQ)$ are the disjoint union $S(P) \sqcup S(Q)$, and $S(P^*)$ is $S(P)$ together with one new element.

results.title: Thompson's construction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: To each regular expression $r$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ it assigns an ε-NFA over $\alpha$ with state set $S(r)$, the states of Thompson's automaton of $r$, by structural recursion: $0$ goes to the automaton with no states, $\varepsilon$ to the one-state automaton, a letter $a$ to the single-letter automaton of $a$, $P + Q$ to the union of the automata of $P$ and $Q$, $PQ$ to their concatenation, and $P^*$ to the…

results.title: Correctness of Thompson's construction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The automaton accepts exactly the words the regular expression matches.

results.title: Thompson state count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The state count $n(r)$ of a regular expression $r$ is defined by structural recursion: $n(0) = 0$, $n(\varepsilon) = 1$, $n(a) = 2$ for a letter $a$, $n(P + Q) = n(P) + n(Q)$, $n(PQ) = n(P) + n(Q)$ and $n(P^*) = n(P) + 1$.

results.title: Number of states of Thompson's automaton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every regular expression $r$, the number of states of Thompson's automaton of $r$ is $n(r)$, the Thompson state count of $r$: $n(0) = 0$, $n(\varepsilon) = 1$, $n(a) = 2$ for a letter $a$, $n(P + Q) = n(P) + n(Q)$, $n(PQ) = n(P) + n(Q)$ and $n(P^*) = n(P) + 1$.

results.title: Normalized heap arity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The normalized arity of a requested arity $r \in \mathbb{N}$ is $\max(2, r)$: the requested arities $0$ and $1$ become $2$ (the binary-heap policy), and every $r \ge 2$ is left unchanged.

results.title: Normalized arities are at least two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $r$, the normalized arity $\max(2, r)$ of $r$ is at least $2$.

results.title: Normalization leaves a valid arity unchanged
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $d \ge 2$, the normalized arity $\max(2, d)$ of $d$ equals $d$.

results.title: Parent index in a $d$-ary tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $i$, the $d$-ary parent of $i$ is $\lfloor (i - 1)/d \rfloor$, computed in the natural numbers: $i - 1$ is truncated at $0$, so the parent of $0$ is $0$, and division by $0$ gives $0$.

results.title: Smallest child in a $d$-ary heap array
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $a$ be an array of length $|a|$ over a linearly ordered type and let $d$ and $i$ be natural numbers. The children of $i$ are the indices $d i + k + 1$ for $0 \le k < d$, and a child is valid when it is below $|a|$. results.title: Extracting the minimum leaves a heap-ordered $d$-ary heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap. If extracting the minimum of $h$ returns a value $x$ and a heap $h'$ of arity $d'$, then $d' \ge 2$ and the storage array $a$ of $h'$ is heap-ordered: for every index $i$ with $0 < i < |a|$, the entry $a_{\lfloor (i-1)/d' \rfloor}$ is at most $a_i$.

results.title: Size of a $d$-ary min-heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type, the number of elements of $h$, counted with multiplicity, equals the length of its backing array.

part.title: Morphogen gradients and the French flag model

path: Morphogen gradients and the French flag model

results.title: Decay length of a morphogen gradient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decay length `λ = √(D / k)` of a morphogen with diffusion coefficient `D` and linear degradation rate `k` (both positive in the model).

results.title: Steady-state exponential morphogen profile
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The steady-state gradient `c(x) = (j / √(D k)) e^{-x/λ}`, `λ = √(D / k)`, for source flux `j` at `x = 0`. Meaningful for `D, k > 0`.

results.title: French-flag boundary position for a threshold
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The French-flag boundary for threshold `θ`: `x_θ = λ log(c(0) / θ)`, where `c(0) = j / √(D k)`. Meaningful for `D, k, j, θ > 0`; it is negative when `θ > c(0)` (no cell is above threshold).

results.title: Bounded steady state of the synthesis–diffusion–degradation model
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A bounded steady state of the synthesis–diffusion–degradation model on `[0, ∞)`, with `c' = dc/dx`: `D c'' = k c` for `x > 0`, `c` and `c'` continuous up to the source, source flux `-D c'(0) = j`, and `c` bounded on `[0, ∞)`.

results.title: Positivity of the decay length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decay length is positive for positive `D` and `k`.

results.title: Diffusion coefficient over squared decay length equals degradation rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `D / λ² = k`.

results.title: Source amplitude in terms of the decay length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `√(D k) = D / λ`, so the source amplitude is `c(0) = j λ / D`.

results.title: Slope of the morphogen profile
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The profile has slope `c'(x) = -c(x)/λ`.

results.title: Exponential profile is a bounded steady state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The exponential profile is a bounded steady state with source flux `j`.

results.title: Uniqueness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every bounded steady state with source flux `j` is the exponential profile on `[0, ∞)`.

results.title: Morphogen profile is strictly decreasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The profile is strictly decreasing in `x` for a positive source.

results.title: Profile equals the threshold at the French-flag boundary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The profile equals `θ` at the boundary `x_θ`.

results.title: French-flag boundary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For positive parameters and threshold `θ`, `c(x) = θ` exactly at `x = x_θ = λ log(c(0)/θ)`.

results.title: French-flag regions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A cell at `x` is at or above threshold `θ` iff it lies within the boundary `x_θ`: `θ ≤ c(x) ↔ x ≤ x_θ`.

results.title: Boundary shift
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Scaling the source flux by `a > 0` moves every French-flag boundary by `λ log a`.

results.title: Doubling the source flux shifts boundaries by $\lambda \log 2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Doubling the source flux shifts every French-flag boundary away from the source by exactly `λ log 2`.
